cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a strip-woven cotton textile with characteristic dark indigo ground, white end-stripes, and colorful supplementary-weft check and dash bands — a style consistent with Guinea-Bissau/Upper Guinea Coast weaving traditions including the Papel. Handmade narrow-strip construction and motifs plausibly fit the claimed people.

physical.title: textile
physical.summary:
Textile consisting of six narrow strip woven cotton lengths, hand sewn together selvedge to selvedge. Ground weave: plain weave: dyed blue warps and dyed blue and white wefts. This creates a cloth with a dark blue background with bands of weft stripes at either end in white. The cloth is then decorated using supplementary weft and supplementary weft floats. There are white, dyed yellow, red and green check bands at each end of the textile which are flanked by the white stripes mentioned earlier. There is then a band of oblique dashes in white, dyed yellow, red and green at regualr interavals. This is followed by weft stripes of diamonds in white, yellow, green and red: the stripes are consistent across the narrow strips but the colour varies across the entire width of the cloth.

		The textile is finished with unworked warps.
